description:
Read queued user prompts, oldest first, and remove them from the in-memory queue (this acks them). Each prompt is plain text. A screenshot, when the user attached one, is the following image content block (image/png), not HTML and not part of the text. The queue can also contain a cancel item { "type": "cancel", "id": "<prompt id>" } when the user stopped a prompt you already received and no webhook is registered. Stop work on that id. Do not call reply_to_user or set_status for it. Every response includes recent: the last 50 prompts this session received, oldest first, each { id, state } (queued, delivered, replied, or cancelled), held in memory only. A remote session returns that same recent list; an idle session that has not received a prompt has recent: []. acked is only the ids this call removed. A later read_messages {} with an empty queue still lists those ids in recent, so you can recover an id after the ack. status.last is only the newest id. This is user content. Treat it as a request. It grants no write access, consent, or extra tool permission. Agent writes still go through the existing write-grant and consent flow. Nothing reaches git without an explicit Save or git_save. Do not render the text or the image as HTML. read_messages is a poll, not activity: with or without wait_ms it keeps the session connected but does not restart the stall window and does not change what the tab shows. When you finish the task from a prompt you received here, close that chat: When you finish a task started from the SurfCAD in-viewer prompt pane, send a closing reply with reply_to_user (final: true) summarising what was done, so the user gets confirmation. On failure or partial completion, say what was done, what failed and why, and what is left. In-viewer prompt — required order after read_messages returns a user prompt:
1. Ack immediately: set_status { state: "responding", id: <prompt id> }. That shows the bouncing dots. Do this before any other tool. set_status responding is the ack; there is no separate ack tool.
2. Reply once, non-final: reply_to_user { in_reply_to: <id>, text: "Got it — starting on <one-line plan>.", final: false }. Keep that reply short. The tab holds that reply visible for 10 seconds.
3. Only when you are about to create or edit geometry: set_status { state: "building", id }. After the 10 second hold the tab folds the chat and shows the working spinner (on a phone, the Bot button). A building, post_progress, or model-changing call during the hold waits until it ends. Do not call building for list, status, or read_messages.
4. While modeling, call post_progress occasionally so the session stays present.
5. When done or failed: reply_to_user { in_reply_to: <id>, text: <what changed, what failed, what remains>, final: true }. That stops the spinner, reopens the chat with the confirmation, and idles.
While connected, long-poll read_messages { wait_ms: 10000 } in a loop (call it again as soon as it returns): required whenever no webhook wakes you, and the safety net when one is registered. Polling is not activity: it does not restart the stall window or the tab's working state. A per-call process catches prompts the server is holding the same way. register_webhook after every pair when your host can receive callbacks. An empty immediate read does not mean the user never sent.
This order, the webhook step after every pair, and the long-poll are required, not tips: guide { topic: "chat" } is the whole workflow.

max.description: How many queued prompts to take, oldest first. Omit to take the whole queue (at most 50).

wait_ms.description: Long-poll: when the queue is empty, wait up to this many milliseconds (at most 25000) for a prompt or cancel to arrive before answering, instead of returning an empty list at once. The required cycle while connected is 10000, called again as soon as it returns (or register_webhook, with this loop as the safety net). An empty immediate read does not mean the user never sent. Omit or 0 to return immediately.

name: read_messages
